spec.title: LangSmith Self-Hosted
spec.description: Operational dashboards for your own LangSmith deployment. Each component requires its documented telemetry collection. Filters select data, not access rights.

options.content: **Self-hosted SmithDB vitals.** Companion to the [SmithDB metrics reference](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics). Scope with the **namespace** variable. Metric names are as SmithDB exposes them on `/metrics`, with no prefix. `langsmith_*` metrics are emitted by LangSmith.

Green means healthy: query and ingest latency flat, pending counts steady, and all four error tiles at zero for the selected time range. Pending compaction jobs and compaction failures are separate signals: jobs can fail while the queue stays flat, and the queue can grow while every job succeeds. [Baseline metrics](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#baseline-metrics)

Emitted by LangSmith, not SmithDB. End-to-end latency is the user-facing number; during dual ingestion compare `store="smithdb"` against `store="clickhouse"`. If **API to worker** rises, the LangSmith queue is the bottleneck, not SmithDB. If **Worker to store** rises, SmithDB writes are slow. [LangSmith ingestion path](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#langsmith-ingestion-path)

spec.title: Queue wait vs store write p95 (smithdb)

options.content: Batch latency is received-to-flushed. Sustained growth in pending entries means flushing is backlogged. A flat flush rate while traffic arrives means writes are not landing. Rising flush duration points at object store latency or undersized ingestion. Permits in use pinned at max means writes are queuing. [Ingestion](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#ingestion)

spec.title: Flush trigger by reason and level
Concurrency permits in use vs max

options.content: Status is the gRPC code; `0` is success. Rising fanout drives both latency and memory, and any sustained rejection rate means queries are failing outright. Peak operator memory approaching the configured limit precedes query termination. [Query](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#query)

spec.title: Scan fanout p95 by query type (top 8)

options.content: Sustained growth in pending jobs means compaction is falling behind. A `job_kind` dropping to zero in completions means that job type has stopped running. Executed persistently below scheduled, or capacity used pinned at the limit, means workers are under-provisioned. Job latency includes queue wait, so it also rises when workers saturate. [Compaction](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#compaction)

Object store latency feeds every flush and compaction; split by op to separate reads from writes. Track resident memory against the pod memory limit. [All components](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#all-components)

spec.title: Object store latency p95 by op

options.content: Prometheus host and optional JuiceFS metrics only; API/APM and provider bucket metrics are not included. Data source and Namespace(s) apply to both tabs; Sandbox cluster applies only here. Select one Sandbox pool for capacity counts. Snapshot gauges require a sample within 60s; trends follow the dashboard range. Empty data is unknown, not zero.
